ai.title: Switch diff expansion to gpt-4o-mini
ai.summary: Backend diff generation now uses gpt-4o-mini via promptOpenAI instead of Claude Haiku. openai-api.ts exposes promptOpenAI accepting dynamic model strings. Scope limited to backend/src/generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts and backend/src/openai-api.ts. sendChatMessage replaced by promptOpenAI to support model parameterization.

eli5.text: The internal tool the system uses to guess missing code now gets its suggestions from a faster, cheaper assistant model instead of its old one. This only affects automated backend diff generation, so you won't notice any change unless you're an admin debugging the service, and even then it's invisible unless that process fails to start today.

ai.title: manicode 1.0.31
ai.summary: Version bump in `npm-app/package.json`. No functional changes. Internal release marker.

eli5.text: Developers working on the assistant marked the version number to 1.0.31 in the project's settings file, which is an internal way of tracking releases. The assistant itself works exactly the same, and you wouldn't see any difference. This change doesn't affect you or any feature you use.

ai.title: Lazy init openai client
ai.summary: OpenAI client initialization moved from module load to `getOpenAI` helper in `backend/src/openai-api.ts`. Defers `Configuration` and `OpenAIApi` construction until `promptOpenAI` executes, preventing startup errors if `OPEN_AI_KEY` is unset. Internal backend refactor only.

eli5.text: When the backend starts up, it no longer tries to talk to the AI provider right away. Instead, it waits until a request actually arrives that needs to use the AI, and only then sets up the connection. This means the system won't crash during startup if the AI key is missing or misconfigured, and the delay only happens once when the first AI request is made.

ai.title: Drop request summary step from system prompt
ai.summary: General case instruction in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` drops step 1 "Summarize the user's request", renumbering remaining steps 2-5 to 1-4. `code_review` block now leads the flow, followed by `brainstorm`, step-by-step reasoning, and knowledge-file edit. Scope: backend system prompt only; six mock-data files under `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/` plus `expansion-diff-prompt.test.ts` added to cover the change.

eli5.text: The assistant now starts by looking at the code changes in your message first, instead of summarizing your request at the beginning. This means the order of its reasoning steps has shifted: it still explores options, explains its plan, and records any lessons learned, but the code review step now leads the process. The change is live today and only affects this internal backend system prompt.

ai.title: Add generate-patch.ts with line ending normalization
ai.summary: New backend/src/generate-patch.ts replaces expansion-only logic with hybrid strategy using LARGE_FILE_CHARACTERS threshold. Normalizes CRLF to LF before processing, restores original line endings in final patch. generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts loses generatePatch export; main-prompt.ts imports from new module. generateExpandedFileWithDiffBlocks added to generate-diffs-prompt.ts for diff-block application.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to rewrite a file, it now follows a smarter two-step editing process instead of one fixed method. If the original file is very large and the new version is much shorter, the assistant applies the changes directly to the original text (preserving its structure) and then converts Windows-style line breaks back to match the original file's format, reducing formatting errors. This improves reliability for large file rewrites but only affects that specific size condition. The change is already live today as part of the assistant's update.

ai.title: Strip leading newline in parseFileBlocks
ai.summary: parseFileBlocks and parseFileBlocksWithoutPath in common/src/util/file.ts now strip leading newlines from parsed file content. Removed verbose prompt logging in backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts. Prevents malformed file content from starting with unnecessary whitespace.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads a file you give it, it used to keep any blank line that appeared at the very top, which could make the file look slightly malformed. Now it quietly removes that single extra leading newline before using the content, so parsed file content starts cleanly. You wouldn't see a new button or message, but any downstream text built from those parsed snippets no longer begins with unexpected whitespace. The change also turned off one noisy internal log line about prompts, leaving only the timing and response details.

ai.title: System prompt clarification on user corrections
ai.summary: System prompt instructions in backend/src/system-prompt.ts updated to clarify knowledge file update triggers. Changed 'did something wrong' to 'corrects you or contradicts you or gives broad advice'. Reordered plan steps to place file editing before final knowledge note.

eli5.text: The instructions that guide your assistant when it writes down things it learns have been tweaked. When you correct the assistant, point out something it got wrong, or offer general advice, it will now treat that as a clear signal to update its notes so it remembers for next time. The order of steps when writing those notes has also been shuffled, so editing files happens before it records what it learned. If you ever check the source notes, you may notice these wording and ordering changes are already in the code, but they only affect how the assistant internally takes direction.

ai.title: Refine diff parsing to strip leading/trailing newlines
ai.summary: Replaced `trim()` with `removeNewlinesFromStartAndEnd()` in `parseAndGetDiffBlocks` within `backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts`. This change preserves internal whitespace and indentation while strictly removing only leading and trailing newlines from search and replace content blocks. Documentation in `backend/knowledge.md` was updated to reflect the two main diff generation strategies. The new helper function uses regex `/^\n+|\n+$/g` to ensure precise content matching for file diffs.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to show you the differences it wants to make in a file, it now keeps the spacing and indentation inside each change exactly as intended instead of accidentally flattening it. You would notice that code blocks and text comparisons look right rather than being oddly rewrapped, because only extra blank lines at the very beginning and end get removed. This affects anyone reviewing the suggested edits before applying them, and it is already live today.

ai.title: system-prompt adds minimal-change guard for code edits
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts gains an instruction telling the agent to assume every line has a purpose and to make only the most minimal change when modifying existing code. The change addresses observed behavior where the agent removed if guards, dropped log/error statements, or added <form> elements beyond the request. musings.knowledge.md records the motivating failure cases alongside the new rule.

eli5.text: When helping make changes to existing code, the assistant will now follow a stricter rule: it assumes every existing line is there for a reason and should only be changed as little as possible to get the job done. This means it won't remove safety checks, delete logging statements, or add extra components unless directly asked. If you looked at the updated instructions, you'd see a new line telling the assistant to minimize changes and preserve the original code's behavior. This change is in place today.

ai.title: Route Claude and OpenAI through Helicone
ai.summary: Backend LLM clients now proxy requests through Helicone. `claude.ts` sets `baseURL` to `anthropic.helicone.ai` and injects `Helicone-Auth`. `openai-api.ts` updates `baseOptions.url` to `oai.hconeai.com/v1` with matching auth headers. Requires `HELICONE_API_KEY` environment variable.

eli5.text: When you use the AI helper, your requests now travel through a service called Helicone before reaching the assistant, so whoever runs the system can see how often it's used and how it's performing. You don't need to do anything differently; your experience stays the same, but the team behind it gains clearer insights into usage and costs. The change is already active today, assuming the system has the required Helicone key configured.

eli5.text: When you start up Manicode, it now checks whether you're running it from the top level of your project. If you're inside a subfolder that doesn't contain the project's main code-tracking directory, it pops a yellow warning telling you to navigate to the root first, preventing the assistant from accidentally working in the wrong location. This check is live today and applies to anyone launching the assistant from their command line.

ai.title: Terminal command handler adds 10s timeout and live output
ai.summary: handleRunTerminalCommand replaces promisify(exec) with spawn to enforce a 10-second MAX_EXECUTION_TIME. Output streams live to process.stdout/stderr via chalk, while a formatResult helper aggregates captured data. Timed-out commands return partial results with a status tag; completed commands include exit_code. The timeout message incorrectly states 2 seconds despite the 10_000ms constant. Scope limited to npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant now runs each terminal command for up to 10 seconds and then stops it, returning whatever output came in during that time. If a command is still running when the limit is reached, it shows a message saying the command timed out (though the message mistakenly says two seconds). Commands that finish on their own will report whether they succeeded by including an exit code. This only affects commands the assistant runs behind the scenes, so you may notice it in any internal log or debug output where those commands appear.

ai.title: License field standardized to UNLICENSED across packages
ai.summary: Root, backend, and common package.json files updated to use "UNLICENSED" instead of "proprietary" or missing values. Aligns licensing metadata with npm conventions for private/unlicensed code. Affects backend/package.json, common/package.json, and package.json. Standardizes the string across the workspace.

eli5.text: The project's license information was made consistent across all its parts, replacing mixed or missing license labels with a single standard value that matches the convention used for private, non-public code. Because the project is already marked as private, this standardization primarily matters to tools and automated systems that read the project metadata, not to how the software runs. If you opened the project's configuration files today, you would see the same license entry everywhere instead of different wording or blanks.

ai.title: Skip file requests for terminal commands and empty results
ai.summary: Added guards in `main-prompt.ts` to return empty strings when `filePaths` or `relevantFiles` are empty, preventing unnecessary context updates. Modified `request-files-prompt.ts` to skip fetching comprehensive file lists if the key file list is empty, and updated the comprehensive model selection to `gpt-4o-mini` via `promptOpenAI`. Prompt instructions now explicitly direct the model to return no files if the user's last message is a terminal command.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a terminal command, it now skips the step of searching through your project files altogether, so responses finish faster and don't accidentally pull in irrelevant file contents. The file-selection step also switched to a cheaper, faster model for its broader searches, and the assistant is explicitly told to return no files at all when your last message is a terminal command. This affects internal backend behavior and is live today.

ai.title: CLI spinner and stream-start callback
ai.summary: npm-app/src/cli.ts replaces the static '...' output with a 100ms spinner and clears it when the response ends or the first streamed chunk arrives. npm-app/src/client.ts adds an onStreamStart callback to subscribeToResponse, fired once for the matching userInputId when the first response-chunk is received. npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts logs the exit code after run_terminal_command closes. The change is scoped to the npm CLI client and tool handler files shown in the diff.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question in the command-line tool, instead of a plain '...' while it thinks, you now see a small spinning animation that runs until the first part of the answer arrives, then clears away as the response streams in. The spinner stops as soon as the assistant starts sending its reply, and a separate log line records the exit code when a terminal command the assistant runs finishes. This only affects the command-line version of the tool and is live today.

ai.title: Improve OpenAI error handling and terminal command prompt
ai.summary: Backend error logging refined in openai-api.ts to extract specific error messages. request-files-prompt.ts now catches errors and returns empty results to prevent crashes. system-prompt.ts updated to clarify terminal command execution behavior.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks its behind-the-scenes helper to fetch relevant files, it now uses a faster, cheaper model and will quietly return an empty list instead of crashing if the helper fails for any reason. Behind the scenes, the assistant also logs more precise error details when it has trouble talking to its helper, and its written instructions now make clear that after running a command you type, it should not add extra explanation on top of the printed result. None of this changes what the assistant looks like to you, but it makes file lookups more reliable and slightly quicker.
